candidates.source_body_excerpt: An increase in absences caused by stress and depression has contributed to more than 30,000 sick days among Rochdale Council staff — and more than £4.2 million in sick pay. Next week, the council’s Employment and Equalities Committee will consider the steps being taken to support staff after figures for 2025-26 show total number of days lost was 30,707.80, which equates to £4,237,676.40 in sick pay. This averages 11.49 days per full-time employee due to sickness absence, with the main reason being stress/depression — an 11.2% increase on the previous year’s total of 10.33 days. The latest figures show that 65% were long-term absences, 35% were short-term absences and both are consistent with figures for previous years. The report says that the council is continuing to support staff with their health and wellbeing, and is providing a programme of initiatives throughout the year. This includes prevention of ill health and promotion of staff wellbeing. Detailed analysis of the 2025/2026 figures show that the main reasons for long-term absence were stress/depression, operative/post-operative and back and sprains, strains, bruises and breaks. For short-term absences, the reasons are stress/depression, colds/flu/viral infections, diarrhoea/ vomiting/sickness bug.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands of people enjoyed Rochdale’s Ignite Fire Festival and the Christmas Lights switch-on. More than 15,000 people attended the three-day event which lead up to the festive switch-on at the town hall on Sunday. Ignite, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK and organised by Rochdale Development Agency, transformed the square and gardens around the town hall into a trail of fire, lights and entertainment. Immersive night-time trail BODY took visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience was the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite was its north-west premiere. Visitors were taken on a dramatic journey as they walked through the glowing embers of human metabolism – the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Visitors arriving at BODY, the trail enjoying its north-west premiere at Ignite Fire Festival There was also a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle and a stunning backdrop, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall. Drum Machine — the 20-strong drumming collective — brought its dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival, performing multiple sets each night.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: More than 100 vehicles were stopped during a clampdown on dangerous and illegal drivers. Greater Manchester Police carried out operations in Rochdale and Middleton yesterday, with Trading Standards and the DVSA. GMP shared: “We operated at three primary locations: Mellor Street, Rochdale; Queensway, Rochdale; and Grimshaw Lane, Middleton, where we stopped 118 vehicles. “Four vehicles were seized due to having no valid insurance, and two arrests were made on suspicion of drug-driving and driving while disqualified.” Officers issued 15 Traffic Offence Reports for various traffic offences, and five stop-searches were conducted under Section 23 of the Misuse of Drugs Act. GMP added: “This operation was initiated following concerns from residents and councillors regarding unsafe driving on these roads. “More operations are planned for the future.” Reacting to the operations, people also identified other areas for police to target.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Joanna Lea was sentenced to two years in prison in relation to child cruelty towards Allister Von Lea in 2022 A Lancashire MP has called for a mother's two-year jail sentence to be reviewed after she admitted child cruelty offences against her three-month-old son before his death. Oliver Ryan, the Labour MP for Burnley, has asked the attorney general to review the sentence handed to Joanna Lea, 36, following her conviction at Preston Crown Court on Monday. Lea, from Rochdale, pleaded guilty to child cruelty offences committed before the death of her son, Allister Von Lea, in August 2022. Post-mortem examinations found cocaine and the anxiety drug pregabalin in Allister's system. Ryan said he was "disgusted" by the cruelty inflicted on the baby and "appalled" by the two-year prison sentence. Emergency services were called to Lea's home in Padiham at about 03:00 BST on 9 August 2022 after reports that Allister was not breathing. He was pronounced dead at hospital a short time later. The court heard that Lea had subjected the infant to a pattern of abuse, including an incident in which she painted a symbol in blood on the baby's head and shared images of it with friends.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: John Morris has long campaigned for a study into the health impacts of Britain's nuclear programme A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment". John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island. It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight . Burnham told campaigners in Downing Street that he would launch an independent investigation Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 2027 Challenge Cup campaign will kick off on the weekend of January 16-17, bringing together clubs from across the rugby league pyramid in a format that celebrates the depth and heritage of the sport, while building towards the ultimate prize at Wembley Stadium. The first round draw will take place on Monday 30 November at Wembley Stadium, live on the newly-launched Challenge Cup YouTube channel. It will feature 28 community clubs, offering teams from across the country a chance to face the professional game's biggest names on the road to the national stadium. A brand-new identity for the Challenge Cup will be unveiled on Monday, signalling the beginning of the competition’s next chapter and providing a distinctive platform to connect with existing supporters, attract new audiences and elevate the competition's profile. The launch will also include the announcement of a new commercial partner and a dedicated ticket sales window, giving rugby league fans an exclusive opportunity to secure their place at Wembley Stadium on Saturday 5 June. Under the revised format, the bottom four Super League teams from 2026, plus newly-promoted London Broncos, will enter in the fourth round, with the remaining top-flight clubs, excluding Catalans Dragons and Toulouse Olympique (who will not participate in 2027), joining in the fifth round. The Challenge Cup will once again start in January with a full round of community club ties, before 10 Championship clubs join in the second round, the remaining 10 joining in the third round. The fourth and fifth rounds will take place in March, followed by the quarter-finals in April and the semi-finals on the weekend of May 8-9. The successful finalists will then have four weeks to prepare for the Challenge Cup Final on Saturday 5 June. The Women's Challenge Cup final will once again take centre stage at Wembley on Saturday 5 June as part of Finals Day, celebrating the continued growth and importance of the women's game. The Wheelchair Challenge Cup final will follow, on the weekend of June 26-27, ensuring the competition's revitalised chapter embraces all forms of the sport.
candidates.source_summary: The Challenge Cup will enter an exciting new era in 2027, with a refreshed format, a bold new identity and a renewed ambition to make one of rugby league's most iconic competitions bigger, more compelling and more accessible to fans.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Under the improved structure, clubs will play 18 league fixtures within their own conference, with nine home games and nine away games, before the top five in each conference progress to the Championship play-offs. A four-week play-off series will build towards a Grand Final scheduled for October 3, while the Shield Trophy will offer a further opportunity for clubs outside the leading places to compete for silverware. The conference model will give clubs a clear route through the regular season, with all 18 league fixtures played against opponents from their own conference. Each club will have nine opportunities to play in front of their home supporters, alongside nine away fixtures, with conference standings determining qualification for the Championship play-offs. The opening conference round is scheduled for January 21–24, with the final round of league fixtures planned for September 2–5. Week 1: The top five teams in both the East and West conferences will reach the play-offs. In week one, fourth will play fifth in each conference for a place in the next round. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Living Well Rochdale has carried out 2,000 free community health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A pioneering football-based project is helping young girls in the borough build confidence, friendships and resilience through the power of sport. Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust and Pennine Care Charity have teamed up with Rochdale AFC Community Trust to deliver a new programme for girls aged six to 11 who are waiting for, or already receiving, support from Rochdale child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). The free 36-week pilot uses fun football activities to help girls stay active and develop their confidence, social skills and emotional wellbeing in a safe and welcoming environment. The programme was developed following feedback from parents of children receiving support from CAMHS, who highlighted the need for activities to help their children build self-esteem and make friends. The project is funded by the Football Association’s Empower Her Fund, which supports opportunities for women and girls to get involved in football. Sessions are delivered by experienced staff from Rochdale AFC Community Trust. Sixteen girls have taken part so far, with early feedback showing how much they are enjoying the sessions and the opportunities to build confidence and make new friends. Anders Cox, clinical lead at Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CAMHS, run by Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust, said: “Getting active, making friends and feeling part of something can all support young people’s mental health. “This project gives the girls a fun and welcoming environment where they can build their confidence, learn new skills and enjoy being active together.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Daalat Ali feared he would never get home after being pulled off a flight back from Pakistan. Rochdale’s deputy council leader was detained twice in 10 days following a civic delegation in the country at the end of October. After touching down in Islamabad on October 19, he was whisked away into a side room by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), Pakistan’s primary federal law-enforcement, border control, and criminal investigation agency. They questioned him about his political background and kept there for around four hours without knowledge as to what was going on. They later took him to a meeting with the High Commissioner – the UK government’s representative – who let him go. The Kingsway ward representative said it was scary at first, but described the authorities as completely professional through the whole process. He joined back up with the Rochdale council delegation in Sahiwal – aimed at bringing closer ties between the two towns. “They didn’t know why they were holding me, “ Coun Ali added. “I went to the immigration desk and something came up on the computer. “We kept asking if I was under arrest and they said no. They didn’t seem to know why when we asked.” But when attempting to return home on October 28 from Lahore airport, the same thing happened again. This was when things really got scary for the Rochdalian.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: 10X Athletic will provide supplements to support the nutritional requirements of the men’s first team across preparation, fuelling, hydration and recovery. Its portfolio includes electrolyte products, protein and recovery formulas and vitamins and minerals. The partnership brings together the club’s professional environment with 10X Athletic’s specialist focus on the nutritional demands of rugby league. The company develops its products with input from nutritionists, sports scientists, coaches and professional players. As part of the new and exciting partnership, 10X Athletic will feature prominently on the men’s first team, women’s and wheelchair kits in 2027, and will help prepare the first team players for the upcoming season, fuelling every session from pre-season through to matchdays. Fans can get in on it too, simply by using code Hornets10 at checkout for 10% off. Danny Lee, Rochdale Hornets head of strength and conditioning, said: “Nutrition plays a vital role in supporting our players’ preparation, performance and recovery. “Having access to products that are third party tested makes them a great choice for drug-tested athletes and are essential in a performance environment.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 28-year-old winger, who joined Town on a one-year deal at the end of the summer transfer window, produced another excellent performance and was on target with a well-taken finish after 11 minutes. “I’ve started to get into a bit of a rhythm now and I’m building those relationships with other players in the team,” said Dale. “My main aim is just to help the team get us to where we want to get to. “I’ve got to credit the boys, I can’t play the way I play without them and what they do behind me, and obviously I’m happy with the goal. “I’ve had a few where I’ve been a bit unlucky and I’ve been critical of myself because I feel I could have had four or five already. But now that first one has gone in hopefully it opens the floodgates.” On how he’s finding life at Sixfields in general, Dale added: “I’m really enjoying myself. The group’s top, as are the manager and the staff, and the way we play really suits me. It allows me to express myself and I’m enjoying being part of this team.” Dale’s goal was the least Cobblers deserved for a dominant first half display but a wobble after half-time put the result in doubt - until Elliott List and Lee Evans turned things around. “It was really important to get the win and obviously I’m happy on a personal note to get off the mark,” Dale continued. “It’s been a few games coming but hopefully I can kick-on and score a few more. “I thought we showed great resilience and the lads did a great job off the bench. We are disappointed with how we started the second half because that should have been a 3-0 game, not 3-2, after how we played in the first half. “We will look back at that and we’ll be critical of ourselves but these things happen and the resilience we showed is a credit to the group and to the manager and the staff and how we’re building. We’re getting better and better.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale have begun the search for Ian Watson’s successor after defeat at Northampton left Dale 22nd. Barnet visit Spotland on Saturday. Rochdale parted company with head coach Ian Watson on Sunday 22 November after a 3-2 defeat at Northampton Town left them 22nd in League Two. The club have begun the search for his successor ahead of Saturday’s home game against Barnet. In their statement on Sunday , Rochdale thanked Watson for his work at the Crown Oil Arena and said the recruitment process was already under way. He leaves five months after taking charge, with Dale two points clear of relegation and four wins from their opening 16 league games. Northampton and Rochdale began Saturday level on points. Two of the players he recalled to the starting line-up, Ed Francis and Cian Hayes, scored within two minutes of each other early in the second half to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. It lasted just 12 minutes. Elliott List equalised before Lee Evans converted the penalty that settled the game, leaving Dale to travel home without a point despite having led with half an hour to play. “We didn’t start the game well at all,” Watson told the club’s post-match interview on Saturday. His departure was announced the following morning. Ian Watson succeeded Jimmy McNulty in June after McNulty guided Rochdale back into the Football League and left for Stockport. The former South Shields manager did take Dale into the second round of the FA Cup , beating Fleetwood 2-1 away earlier this month. Two League Two fixtures come before the home cup tie against Newport on 5 December. Barnet visit first, followed by a trip to Cheltenham on Tuesday 1 December.
